subject: plotmath expressions - different behavior on server vs. local host

messages.author: 2dc50513792871a4
messages.subject: plotmath expressions - different behavior on server vs. local host
parts:
Hi,

I have an example Shiny app here that I am working on:
http://shiny.snap.uaf.edu/RV_distributionsV4/

I have added probability density and mass functions to my plots using plotmath expressions. What I have found is that when I run the app on my pc using local host, the expressions plot nicely. However, once that app is run using shiny-server, the notation is not so nice, particularly with commas and minus signs and such overlapping with other text and symbols and being in the wrong place in the displayed equations. For example, if you click on the normal distribution at the link above and look at the displayed pdf and support, you can see the issue.

Normally I would just dig into my code and see what is wrong, and perhaps there is a better way I can make an expression, but I feel like on a fundamental level, there should be nothing necessarily wrong with the R code, as the same code from the version of the same copy of the app I have on github, displays properly using local host but a bit messy using shiny-server. Please let me know if code would be helpful or anything else I can provide. Does anyone know of why this different plotmath behavior may be occurring? I've attached a screenshot of how the plot annotation displays when I run the same app using a local host.

Thanks,
Matt

parts:
One more thing I forgot to mention. At the link above, the 'download graphic' button, which generates a pdf of the currently displayed plot, still works properly and gives the user a pdf of the plot with nice annotation. Interestingly, the plot in the browser and the plot made using pdf() make use of the same plotting code, albeit with some slightly different par(margin=c()) settings.

Matt

messages.subject: Re: plotmath expressions - different behavior on server vs. local host
parts:
No special fonts. As an example, the expression for the normal distribution is as follows:

cexpr.norm <- expression(
italic(
paste(
displaystyle(f(x)~"="~frac(1,sqrt(2*pi*sigma^scriptscriptstyle("2")))~e^{frac(-1,2*sigma^{scriptscriptstyle("2")})*(x-mu)^scriptscriptstyle("2")})
~~~~displaystyle(list(paste(-infinity<x) <infinity, atop(paste(-infinity<mu) <infinity, paste(0<sigma^scriptscriptstyle("2")) <infinity)))
)
)
)

I'm not sure I even went about it the best way. The expression is certainly a mess to look at. Apologies for that if there is a way to make it simpler. But I developed the app on my 32-bit Windows 7 pc and a Mac OSX 10.7.5 MacBook Pro, back and forth via github. I have the same distinction between server display and local host display with either system.

Thanks,
Matt

parts:
I just tried using that expression in generating a PNG, using png() and CairoPNG() from the Cairo package, on Linux.

By default, if you have the Cairo package installed, it will use CairoPNG() instead of png(), because the former has better support for antialiasing, so the output generally looks better. Unfortunately, the math expressions look worse with CairoPNG() -- on Linux, at least.

I'd recommend uninstalling the Cairo package and seeing if that helps.


Here's the code I used, and I've attached the output files.


library(Cairo)

I just tried using that expression in generating a PNG, using png() and CairoPNG() from the Cairo package, on Linux.

By default, if you have the Cairo package installed, it will use CairoPNG() instead of png(), because the former has better support for antialiasing, so the output generally looks better. Unfortunately, the math expressions look worse with CairoPNG() -- on Linux, at least.

library(Cairo)

cexpr.norm <- expression(
  italic(
    paste(
displaystyle(f(x)~"="~frac(1,sqrt(2*pi*sigma^scriptscriptstyle("2")))~e^{frac(-1,2*sigma^{scriptscriptstyle("2")})*(x-mu)^scriptscriptstyle("2")})
      ~~~~displaystyle(list(paste(-infinity<x) <infinity, atop(paste(-infinity<mu) <infinity, paste(0<sigma^scriptscriptstyle("2")) <infinity)))
    )
  )
)

png('math_png.png')
matplot(1:4,1:4, main = cexpr.norm)
dev.off()

CairoPNG('math_CairoPNG.png')
matplot(1:4,1:4, main = cexpr.norm)
dev.off()

-Winston
